constructor_evidence.result: invocation_temp is generated with rand::rng().next_u32() only when sess.opts.incremental is Some. No save-temps, emit, or debuginfo condition disables that random generation.

options.name: Disable incremental compilation with supported Cargo profile/environment control
options.control: CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 globally, or documented incremental=false profile settings
options.effect: No rustc incremental path should be supplied, so the constructor produces None and does not append random invocation_temp suffix. Actual verbose rustc argv must verify no -C incremental.
cautions: Default codegen units change from256 incremental to16 nonincremental; a global256 override would also change external dependencies previously nonincremental.
The frozen manifest dependency opt-level=3 must remain unchanged.
Incremental compilation strategy can affect code generation and object layout. Retaining language-level settings is not proof of identical visual behavior; paired validation remains required.

options.name: Standard profile strip=debuginfo
options.effect: Documented Cargo control maps to rustc strip, independent of debug-assertions. On pinned Darwin rustc, link.rs1530–1535 invokes external rust-objcopy --strip-debug after linking.
cautions: Adds an externally invoked tool requiring identity/pinning and raw receipt.
Changes debug-map/backtrace/debugger artifact semantics; no claim that this is acceptable for the reference build.
No post-hoc stripping of existing sealed binaries is authorized.

options.name: save-temps or emit changes
options.effect: Not a supported way to disable invocation_temp while incremental remains enabled.
cautions: Object retention/output changes do not remove the constructor random branch.
Manual relinking, compiler patches, or binary normalization are outside the reviewed recipe.

 The  strip  option controls the  -C strip  flag , which directs rustc to
strip either symbols or debuginfo from a binary. This can be enabled like so: 
 [package]
# ...

[profile.release]
strip = "debuginfo"
 
 Possible string values of  strip  are  "none" ,  "debuginfo" , and  "symbols" .
The default is  "none" . 
 You can also configure this option with the boolean values  true  or  false .
 strip = true  is equivalent to  strip = "symbols" .  strip = false  is
equivalent to  strip = "none"  and disables  strip  completely.

 strip 
 The option  -C strip=val  controls stripping of debuginfo and similar auxiliary
data from binaries during linking. 
 Supported values for this option are: 
 
 none  - debuginfo and symbols are not modified. 
 debuginfo  - debuginfo sections and debuginfo symbols from the symbol table
section are stripped at link time and are not copied to the produced binary.
This should leave backtraces mostly-intact but may make using a debugger like
gdb or lldb ineffectual. Prior to 1.79, this unintentionally disabled the
generation of  *.pdb  files
